mike: quick heads-up — longctx load test (~65k tokens ctx) shows KV reuse collapse after ~6m. hit rate drops, memory climbs, eviction spikes in the hot span. profiler attached.
anya: ugh, similar to last month's compaction churn? or different footprint?
mike: superficially similar but traces differ — we're seeing many tiny free/alloc cycles and high fragmentation (frag_ratio reported by kv-stats). looks like keys are short-lived but the pages aren't coalescing.
jordan: can you paste kv-stats + sample key fingerprints and routing info? are requests landing on multiple execs (cross-process) or staying sticky?
mike: paste below — this is from a failing canary host.
```
# kv-stats dump (hotspan)
total_pages: 125430
frag_ratio: 0.62
evictions/sec: 42
avg_page_use: 3.2kB
active_keys: 48.9k
most_evicted_key_prefix: 0x7f2a9c
page_compactions: 1200/min
allocation_pattern: many small allocations (~128B-2KB)
```
lee: that frag_ratio is brutal. any pattern on key shapes? repeated varying suffixes?
mike: yes — keys look like stable prompt fingerprint + appended ephemeral `session_id` or `request_nonce`. so reuse is broken because the key includes per-request metadata.
anya: that's a classic anti-pattern: cache keyed on ephemeral fields. are clients adding anything to the prefix on purpose?
mike: checked client side; they tack on a `session_id` for tracing. server-side key derivation currently includes the entire prompt metadata blob.
jordan: fix options: 1) canonicalize cache-key to fingerprint only (strip session fields) 2) keep a small session-scoped cache for per-session private KV entries 3) adaptive stickiness window (keep mapping from canonical->live key for N seconds to avoid correctness issues).
lee: also consider TTL for ephemeral entries so they don't fragment memory long-term. fragmentation is mostly from many tiny pages becoming live/dead. compaction is expensive and moves memory around which can spike latency.
mike: I ran a quick experiment: branch `hotspan/stickiness-30s` — we canonicalize keys but maintain a short sticky alias for 30s so ongoing session requests still hit exact entries while allowing cross-session reuse after the window. perf-bot deployed canary to 3/5 hosts at 2175000100.
perf-bot: canary deploy hotspan/stickiness-30s -> hosts: canary-3 (3/5) at 2175000100 :rocket:
jordan: results?
mike: early numbers: evictions down ~70% on canary, frag_ratio dropped to 0.28, memory growth flattens. downside: slightly higher P99 generation latency on certain short-batch workloads (we lose some cross-session batching because of aliasing logic).
anya: tradeoff seems acceptable for longctx workloads. but we should make stickiness adaptive: if batch coalescing metric > threshold then shrink window to 0 to maximize batching; if churn high, expand window up to 60s.
lee: also look at kernel-level compaction: we saw stalls when compaction moved pages across NUMA nodes. maybe change compaction to prefer in-place merging or background defrag with rate limit.
mike: good call — filed INF-4821: "hotspan aliasing + compaction stalls investigation" and linked profiler traces + canary numbers.
jordan: propose follow-ups: - short-term: merge canonical-key + adaptive-stickiness feature flag (default 30s) - medium: server-side lint to reject ephemeral fields in cache-key derivation; provide helper `kv_key_stable()` - long-term: change compaction to background, NUMA-aware pass.
anya: I'll take the server-side lint/SDK helper (PR inbound).
lee: I'll prototype NUMA-aware compaction knobs and a rate limiter for page moves.
mike: I'll extend the telemetry to emit "alias_hit" vs "canonical_hit" and batch-coalescing metric so we can drive the adaptive heuristic.
perf-bot: created ticket INF-4821 and INF-4822 (telemetry) at 2175000350
anya: noted. small thumbs-up if you're blocked: :thumbsup:
mike: thanks — rolling to full canary after we validate adaptive window doesn't regress P99 more than 5%. will post numbers.
jordan: also add a quick test that simulates many ephemeral suffixes to ensure we don't regress under adversarial clients.
mike: agreed — test plan in the ticket.
lee: good thread.
perf-bot: canary metrics snapshot attached (2175000600).
mike: closing loop later today with perf graphs. thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
